To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a method based upon the inversion of a three-dimensional interception model that allows us to reconstruct the within-canopy radiative regime and to predict the photosynthetic performance of the canopy.

(1) a new method was developed to estimate three architectural properties of shoots (angular distribution and spatial aggregation of needle area, needle area density) from measurements of needle area and silhouette area for different angles; (2) this methodology was applied to a set of silver fir shoots, and the results showed a large variation in the architectural features along the vertical profile of the canopy; and (3) this methodology can be applied to reconstruct the radiation regime of the shoot, and to up-scale photosynthesis

the shoot architecture of silver fir is characterized by a strong vertical gradient in needle area density, a strong azimuthal gradient in needle area angular distribution, and a strong vertical gradient of clumping.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new approach to estimate the within-canopy light regime in conifer shoots, and to use it for the estimation of canopy photosynthesis and transpiration at the shoot scale.
the application of the turbid medium model for the estimation of shoot architecture and light interception in conifer shoots.
the structural acclimation of shoots in response to light gradients and the radiation regime of silver firs in a mixed forest.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method provides a powerful tool to describe the within-shoot radiation regime, which is an important step towards the upscaling of photosynthesis at the canopy level.
the shoot model developed here can be effectively applied to the reconstruction of the within-shoot radiation regime.
the model is a useful tool in the study of the structural acclimation and light regime of shoots in the field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have been able to develop and test an efficient method for the estimation of the three-dimensional structure of shoots, which can be used for the prediction of the light field inside the shoots and the estimation of photosynthetic capacity.
, in order to estimate the light regime within a shoot, a three-dimensional shoot model is required, which includes the estimation of the shoot architecture and of the light extinction coefficient.

the proposed approach allows the estimation of shoot structure and the within-shoot radiation regime, and provides an important step towards the upscaling of photosynthesis from shoots to the canopy level.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a simple model, which takes into account the three-dimensional needle distribution and clumping, can be used for the prediction of the within-shoot radiation regime, and can be used for a more realistic simulation of canopy photosynthesis.
the shoot model can be used to predict the radiative regime of a shoot and the potential for photosynthesis.
, in addition to shoot dimensions, the angular and spatial distribution of the needle area must be considered in order to estimate the light regime of the shoots.
